mechanism_narrative: Workplaces mobility has risen steadily for three consecutive weeks (-41.7 to -19.7), reflecting progressive return of in-person work and weekday commuting; this recovery will continue to lift weekday retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -41.7 to -19.7 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is not higher than its last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise for at least two more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As RESIDENTIAL time-at-home index falls below a low threshold, it signals that stay-at-home behavior has largely unwound, freeing discretionary time for shopping and leisure trips; a further decline under 1.5 should accelerate retail recovery over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 1.5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 4.7 to 1.4 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks even though RESIDENTIAL drops below 1.5 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates restored commuting infrastructure use; the joint effect compounds retail footfall more than either series alone, because commuters combine trips with errands and shopping on the way to or from work.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have risen every week for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean stays flat or declines even as both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue to rise jointly.

mechanism_narrative: High and rising PARKS mobility during the current season indicates residents favor outdoor recreation and parks substitute for indoor retail and recreation visits; in a warm-season regime this substitution effect will suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remains above 60 points throughout the snapshot
regime_hint: warm season reopening with high outdoor substitution
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even while PARKS remains elevated (>60) throughout, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES growth stalls (week-on-week change falls below 2 points) it signals that commuting recovery has plateaued, possibly due to a policy pause or capacity cap on business reopening, which will stall retail footfall growth within the coming week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change falls below 2 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES week-on-week change decelerated from 13.7 to 7.4 to 0.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next week even though WORKPLACES week-on-week change falls below 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has turned positive and stabilized near +10%, while RETAIL_REC remains negative; the gap between essential and discretionary spending categories should narrow as consumer confidence normalizes, pulling RETAIL_REC upward toward GROCERY_PHARM's level over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM turned positive (+11.3) while RETAIL_REC remains negative (-4.1)
failure_condition: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC widens rather than narrows over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC has been decelerating for three consecutive periods (11.9, 8.1, 3.2 points); if this deceleration continues at the same rate, weekly gains will turn negative within two weeks, causing the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean to fall short of the last 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week increase falls below 1 point
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly increments decelerated from 11.9 to 8.1 to 3.2
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's week-on-week increase remains above 1 point for the next two weeks, i.e., the deceleration trend reverses.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized slowdown across TRANSIT and WORKPLACES growth, combined with still-rising PARKS mobility, would indicate a policy tightening targeted at indoor and workplace activity while outdoor movement remains permitted; this regulatory asymmetry would suppress retail recovery even as other indices stay strong.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES week-on-week gains both fall below 3 points while PARKS continues rising
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES weekly gain fell to 0.9 while PARKS rose to 68.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES growth stalling and PARKS continuing to rise.
